title: Vendor Availability & Degraded-Service Credit Schedule (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This draft sets out a negotiable schedule for calculating availability-based service credits and the operational procedures for degraded-service scenarios when Redwood Inference consumes third-party vendor services that materially affect customer-facing inference availability. It is intended to be embedded into vendor agreements or attached as a standalone schedule.

Scope and intent (short):
- Apply to vendor-hosted or vendor-managed services that materially affect API latency, API success rate, or throughput for customer traffic (examples: model-hosting, routing/control-plane, cache layers).
- Provide a clear measurement methodology, an evidence checklist for customers to claim credits, and a short remediation/termination roadmap for persistent degradation.
- Complement (not replace) security incident obligations and data-privacy commitments. Credits are a remedy for availability only, not a substitute for incident remediation or indemnity where applicable.

Definitions (for schedule):
- Availability: Percentage of successful requests within the defined API surface for the month, measured as: ((Total valid requests - Failed requests - Timed-out requests) / Total valid requests) * 100, where valid requests exclude scheduled maintenance windows and pre-excluded traffic classes.
- Degraded Service: A state where request latency or error rate exceeds the thresholds in the Service Levels and causes increased customer-perceived failures or missing throughput guarantees.
- Downtime Window: A contiguous period during which Availability is below 95% for the affected API(s).
- Rolling Measurement Period: 30-calendar-day period ending on the last day of the invoice month (unless otherwise defined by the Master Agreement).
- Eligible Customer Traffic: Production traffic from Redwood customer-facing endpoints. Synthetic or internal test traffic is excluded unless mutually agreed and instrumented into the measurement set.

Service Levels (examples — negotiable):
- API Success Rate SLA: 99.95% availability per month (measured as defined above).
- P50 latency SLA: <= 80 ms. P95 latency SLA: <= 400 ms. These latency SLAs are measured on upstream vendor ingress-to-egress for production requests routed via Redwood control-plane.
- Throughput SLA (optional, by bundle): Sustained throughput of X requests/sec for a pinned capacity pool under Dedicated arrangements; for hosted arrangements provide baseline capacity targets and burst handling commitments.

Credit Schedule (monthly, cumulative):
- If Availability >= 99.95%: no credit.
- If Availability >= 99.5% and < 99.95%: 5% service credit on the vendor fees attributable to the impacted API for the month.
- If Availability >= 98.0% and < 99.5%: 15% service credit.
- If Availability >= 95.0% and < 98.0%: 30% service credit.
- If Availability < 95.0%: 60% service credit and Redwood may (a) require an agreed remediation plan within 10 business days and (b) if not satisfied, exercise termination for material breach with pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the remainder of committed term.

Calculation principles and allocation: 
- Credits apply only to fees paid for the impacted service component. The vendor must provide a mapping table that ties billable line items to measurable API endpoints or capacity pools.
- Credits are not cumulative across different measurement categories (e.g., latency-driven and availability-driven credits for the same event: apply the single larger credit).
- The calendar month is the billing month unless invoice period differs by contract.

Exclusions (non-exhaustive):
- Scheduled maintenance that was notified according to the agreed maintenance notification windows (see Maintenance & Change Control).
- Force majeure events (as defined in the primary agreement).
- Customer-caused failures, misconfiguration, or traffic patterns outside normal use (DDoS attributable to customer origin, for instance).
- Upstream provider outages that the vendor can demonstrate were completely out of vendor control AND which the vendor promptly and publicly reported with relevant evidence; in those cases, credits may be reduced proportionally.

Measurement & instrumentation (requirements for vendor):
- Measurement endpoint: vendor shall export per-request telemetry (timestamps, request-id, result code, latency) to a secure, vendor-provided metrics stream for the measurement window and provide aggregated reports in machine-readable CSV/JSON.
- Sampling and retention: vendor shall retain raw telemetry for at least 90 days and aggregated metrics for 2 years. Vendor must permit access to relevant aggregates and a defined slice of raw telemetry for audit purposes (see Evidence & Audit).
- Time synchronization: vendor telemetry must use NTP/UTC timestamps; drift > 5s must be disclosed and corrected.

Evidence & acceptance process (how Redwood claims a credit):
- Step 1: Redwood submits a Notice of Degradation within 10 business days of detecting a suspect month-level shortfall. Notice must include preliminary aggregates and affected endpoints.
- Step 2: Vendor has 5 business days to acknowledge and provide initial raw telemetry access or a counter-aggregate. If vendor disputes calculation, the parties exchange measurement artifacts (CSV, query definitions, endpoints).
- Step 3: Parties have 15 business days from acknowledgment to reconcile metrics. If reconciled in Redwood’s favor, credit is applied to the next invoice cycle as outlined in the Credit Schedule.
- Dispute escalation: unresolved disagreements escalate to named technical leads within 5 business days and then to executive-level dispute resolution after an additional 10 business days.

Evidence checklist (minimum deliverables vendor must provide upon request):
- Aggregated request counts per minute per endpoint for the rolling measurement period.
- Per-request sampling (minimum 5% uniformly sampled, or full capture if requested for a 7-day window during dispute): timestamps, request-id, route, upstream result codes, end-to-end latency, and error classification where applicable.
- Server-side logs showing resource pressure events (GC pauses, OOMs, GPU preemption, disk I/O saturation) for the impacted instances during the window.
- Autoscaling and capacity logs (scaling events, queue lengths).
- Notification and maintenance history for the period.

Audit rights and forensic access:
- Redwood may initiate a targeted audit once per 12-month period or upon reasonable suspicion of systemic measurement misreporting. Audit scope limited to evidence for the disputed measurement periods only.
- Audits are interactive: vendor may redact customer-identifiable data; audit operator will execute pre-agreed audit queries on vendor infrastructure or on a mutually agreed staging copy.
- If an audit determines vendor misreporting or withheld evidence materially changed the credit outcome, vendor pays for the audit and doubles the originally determined credit (capped at 100% for the month).

Notification & remediation timeline (operational):
- Initial detection: Redwood notifies vendor support + named account contact within 24 hours of a severity-1 incident affecting production availability.
- Root cause update: vendor must provide an initial RCA window estimate within 3 business days, and a substantive interim status every 48 hours until resolved.
- Final RCA: delivered within 15 business days of incident closure unless extended by mutual agreement; corrected RCA should include mitigation steps to avoid recurrence.

Maintenance & change control (minimum entitlements):
- Planned maintenance windows must be communicated at least 7 days in advance for non-critical changes and 48 hours for hotfixes; emergency maintenance must be communicated as soon as possible with justification. Maintenance windows must be scheduled during low-traffic windows agreed in the SOW where feasible.
- Vendor must maintain a public maintenance calendar with entries linked to relevant change IDs (or provide programmatic feed).

Remedies, limits, and interplay with other obligations:
- Credits are the exclusive monetary remedy for availability failures except where vendor breach also triggers indemnity, data breach, or other damages under the primary agreement.
- Nothing in this schedule limits Redwood’s termination rights for repeated breaches or other contractual remedies for non-availability harms (e.g., data loss).

Sample notice template (for Redwood legal/ops):
- Subject: Notice of Monthly Availability Shortfall — [Service] — [Month YYYY]
- Body: Short description of suspected shortfall, affected endpoints, attached preliminary aggregates, request for vendor acknowledgement within 5 business days, and proposed reconciliation timeline.

Example calculations (illustrative):
- Example A: 10,000,000 valid requests in month. Vendor reports 9,997,000 successful requests (3,000 failed/timed out). Availability = (10,000,000 - 3,000)/10,000,000 = 99.97% → no credit.
- Example B: 10,000,000 valid requests; 55,000 failed/timed out → Availability = 99.45% → falls in 99.5–99.95% bracket → 5% credit on impacted fees.

Open questions and negotiation points (for internal review):
- Whether to cap cumulative credits per rolling 12-month period (recommended: 60% cap aggregated).
- Whether latency-only degradations (without success-rate impact) should have a separate micro-credit schedule (current draft treats latency credits as non-cumulative with availability credits).
- Exact sample rate for per-request evidence vs cost burden on vendor; propose default 5% with rights to request targeted full-capture for up to 7 days per dispute.

Operational notes (practical):
- Keep a small working set of sample queries and synthetic probes in Redwood’s monitoring that mirror production routing to fast-flag candidate months for review.
- Track vendor release windows and known risky changes; tie to post-release watch windows where stricter short-term credits may apply for high-risk releases.

Appendix A — Draft clause language (to drop into SOW or Schedule):
"The Vendor shall maintain the Service in accordance with the Service Levels set out in this Schedule. If the Vendor fails to meet the Service Levels for a Measurement Period, Redwood shall be entitled to the Service Credits specified in the Credit Schedule. For the avoidance of doubt, Service Credits are Redwood's sole and exclusive monetary remedy for any unavailability of the Service except to the extent the failure gives rise to other remedies (such as indemnity) under the Agreement. To claim Service Credits Redwood shall follow the Evidence & Acceptance Process set out in this Schedule."

Appendix B — Evidence handback quick checklist (for ops handoff):
- Who to call (vendor oncall + named contacts)
- Minimum telemetry export format (CSV headers and examples)
- Retention endpoints and service ID mapping table request template

Revision history & notes:
- v0.1 (2025-11-12) Initial draft (Karen Li)
- v0.2 (2026-02-15) - added audit language and double-credit penalty for misreporting (Diego)
- v0.3 (2026-03-10) - clarified sample-capture defaults and notification timing (Samir)

Draft author notes / negotiating playbook (private):
- Push for per-month credit caps, but maintain an escalation pathway to terminate after repeated <95% months in a 6-month window.
- Favor reasonably low evidence-sampling defaults to reduce vendor pushback; retain explicit right to request full capture in dispute windows.
- Coordinate early with product/infra to map billing line items to measurable service IDs before contract signature.

Unresolved items for legal review:
- Exact cap language and whether to link to indemnity carveouts.
- Whether to permit Redwood to aggregate credits across related vendor services when the outage is caused by a shared underlying component.

End of draft.
